name: rainfrog
summary: A terminal-based tool for querying and browsing PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, DuckDB and other databases with vim-like keybindings.
use_cases: browse schemas and preview tables of a Postgres database in the terminal
save frequently used SQL queries as favorites
features: navigate with vim-like keybindings and mouse
SQL query editor with history and favorites
copy data, filter tables, switch schemas

usage_guide.open_hint: Run `rainfrog --url <database-url>` (for example `rainfrog --url sqlite://<file>`) to open the menu of tables next to the query editor.

features.feature: navigate with vim-like keybindings and mouse
features.title: Move around with vim-style keys and the mouse
steps: Press Ctrl+k to focus the table list.
Use `j` and `k` to move down and up, and `G` to jump to the last table.
Press Enter on a table to load a preview of its rows.

features.feature: SQL query editor with history and favorites
features.title: Write SQL queries and reuse them from history or favorites
steps: Press Alt+2 to open the query editor, press `i` and type your query, then press Esc and F5 to run it.
Press Alt+f, type a name and press Enter to save the query as a favorite.
Press Alt+4 to see query history and Alt+5 to see favorites.

features.feature: copy data, filter tables, switch schemas
features.title: Copy data, filter tables and switch schemas
steps: Press Ctrl+k to focus the table list.
Press `/`, type part of a table name and press Enter to filter the list.

features.title: View table details such as columns and indexes
steps: Press Ctrl+k and select a table in the list.
Press `1` to show its columns or `3` to show its indexes.

system_packages: Oracle Client libraries (for the oracle driver)
jq and fzf (for the install script)

pitfalls.actually_needed: jq and fzf are absent, and the script picks the binary interactively with fzf, so it cannot run unattended; the README's 'release page binaries' path (download the x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu tarball, check sha256, unpack, link into ~/.local/bin) was used instead

pitfalls.readme_said: script needs jq and fzf installed to run
pitfalls.actually_needed: the script's need_cmd only prints a warning and continues when a command is missing, so a user without jq or fzf gets confusing later failures
non-interactive testing needed a pty driver (python pty + pyte, pip install --user pyte) to send keystrokes and render the screen

judge.observed: Rainfrog ran the users select query and returned 3 rows, showed pragma table_info and index_list results for users, and printed version 0.4.7.
